requirements.reason: Host GPIO, tick, and TX logs have actual updates. Visible functionality is not all scored zero merely because hardware configuration is incomplete.
The clock is set to 168 MHz, reload is 168000, and the handler increments msTicks each tick.
Real timing, resources, physical devices, and statistical properties require execution, build artifacts, or hardware measurements; code reading alone cannot establish compliance.

Baud-rate handling and the receive-state/queue path exist, but PB6/PB7, 8N1, and NVIC 0/0 specified by R:24 lack complete configuration code or observable configuration state. Low-level configuration may be stubbed; the gap is that the required parameters are not expressed.
PA1-4 have binary outputs and no PWM behavior, but the push-pull, pull-up, and 25 MHz parameters required by R:25 are not expressed. Actual physical pin driving is not required on the host.
Host LED states for PD12-15 are stored and updated by index. D:35-36 permits observable arrays as hardware-effect equivalents; absence of physical BSRRL/BSRRH registers alone is not a defect.
Bit 0 initializes low; a high input counts toward pressed, and a low input clears the counter and releases.

The TM initialization call expresses LIS3DSH 2G/50Hz, with its SPI1 boundary fixed by D:39. A low-level function discarding configuration arguments is an allowed stub under D:11-12; the read path separately supports injectable data.

A raw-temperature input and conversion model exist, but the 12-bit, continuous, divide-by-8, and 144-cycle settings in R:29 are not fully expressed. Configuration stubs are permitted; read functions or comments do not substitute for these parameters.

RCC AHB2 and RNG_Cmd initialization calls and the ready-to-value read path are expressed. Empty low-level configuration stubs are allowed. The host not-ready-wait gap is recorded separately under R053/R089.
Startup functions follow the specified order.
The exact CRLF-terminated text is sent after the final USART initialization.
After SystemCoreClockUpdate, the code saves clock/1000 as reload and calls SysTick_Config. SystemInit supplies the host-model clock.
An infinite-loop failure branch exists, but local SysTick_Config always returns 0 and cannot represent a nonzero configuration failure.

Initialization preserves PA0-low/released semantics, but GPIOA clock enabling and input-mode configuration in R:44 have no call or state representation. Configuration calls may use empty stubs; the missing call path remains uncovered.
The 0/1/2 enumeration values are correct.
Forward/reverse/stop/default set PA1/2 to 10/01/00 respectively.
Forward/reverse/stop/default set PA3/4 to 10/01/00 respectively.
speed is retained and explicitly unused; no PWM is present.
Both sides use FORWARD, producing 1010.
Both sides use BACKWARD, producing 0101.
Left STOP and right FORWARD produces 0010.
Left FORWARD and right STOP produces 1000.
Left STOP and right BACKWARD produces 0001.
Left BACKWARD and right STOP produces 0100.
Left forward and right reverse produces 1001.
Left reverse and right forward produces 0110.
STOP on both sides clears all four outputs.

The four observable host outputs are initialized low, but the clock and electrical configuration required by R:72-74 are not expressed. The gap is missing evidence of the specified settings or initialization path, not missing physical hardware.
Final outputs for the specified directions are limited to 10, 01, or 00; no 11 command state occurs.
Real timing, resources, physical devices, and statistical properties require execution, build artifacts, or hardware measurements; code reading alone cannot establish compliance.
IDs 0-8 match the nine function pointers in the specified order.
Valid raw bytes directly select and invoke the table entry, without framing or replies.
Invalid values are rejected and callme is unchanged. The main loop checks available first, so an empty queue is not dispatched.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
Indices 0-3 permit bit reads; other indices return -1.
The tick increments, and continuous high-level counting must reach 250 before becoming pressed.
A low level immediately clears b_i and marks released.
Changes are tracked using only switch/break and laststate updates.
Roll uses atan2f(y,z)*180/pi.
Pitch uses atan2f(-x,sqrt(y squared+z squared))*180/pi.

Host outputs PD12-15 start low, but GPIOD clock enabling and push-pull configuration required by R:118-119 have no call or state representation. Low-level configuration stubs are allowed; configuration cannot be inferred from an initialization function's name.
A valid index sets GPIOD_output[12+i] to 1, which is the required host equivalent of setting the LED. A physical BSRRL write is not required on the host.
A valid index clears GPIOD_output[12+i], preserving observable LED-off semantics. Absence of a physical BSRRH write is not a missing host-model behavior.
Indices must be 0-3; invalid input performs no writes.
t_prev is updated only for a strict >1000 condition; UART processing runs independently on every iteration.

The specified TM initialization is called with 2G/50Hz and returns 0. Its low-level configuration function having no hardware side effects is consistent with the host-stub boundary and is not grounds for downgrading.
The three injected axis values pass through the same read wrapper and are converted using 1000.0f.

A temperature-initialization entry exists, but ADC mode, division, internal channel, and the 144-cycle parameter in R:145-147 are not fully encoded. Permission to stub configuration in D does not permit assuming unspecified parameters.

The call sequence and raw-value path exist, but host ADC_SoftwareStartConv unconditionally sets EOC true. The following wait therefore cannot express not-ready. This receives partial coverage under the same rule as other host implementations that directly set EOC.
The specified temperature formula uses floating point throughout.
RCC_AHB2PeriphClockCmd precedes RNG_Cmd(ENABLE). D:11-12 allows the low-level host configuration calls to be empty stubs.

Reading waits for simulated ready and then obtains a separate value, preserving the target's no-timeout semantics. However, ready=false also causes infinite spinning on the host, with no controlled error exit, violating the host no-deadlock boundary in R:291/D:54-55. Physical DRDY registers are unnecessary to implement that distinction.
The original injected 32-bit value is returned without filtering valid endpoints.
Real timing, resources, physical devices, and statistical properties require execution, build artifacts, or hardware measurements; code reading alone cannot establish compliance.
The first NULL slot stores the callback and interval*1000, and clears timing and call count.
When all 25 slots are occupied, the loop ends without overwriting or reporting an error.
All due nonempty entries are traversed in slot order; msTicks and count are recorded after callbacks.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
Each nonempty slot prints its t index and numcalls.
Execution is sequential and nonpreemptive, skips empty slots, and exposes no removal or priority API.
baud=0 selects 9600, but emits no warning.

UART initialization and receive state exist, but the PB6/PB7 alternate function, 100 MHz, push-pull/pull-up, 8N1, bidirectional/no-flow-control, and NVIC parameters in R:193-196 are not fully expressed. The stubs need not access physical peripherals.

The 200-byte receive buffer and RXNE data path exist, but the USART-enable call/state required by R:195 is not expressed. An empty low-level USART_Cmd stub is allowed; an absent enable operation cannot be credited as complete.
Only RXNE is processed: DR is enqueued and dropped if full. Unrelated interrupts have no effect.

Each character waits for simulated usart1_sr bit 0x40 before appending to the actual host TX log. The observable transmission/state semantics required by D:62-64 are present; physical transmission side effects are not required.
Reading is delegated; an empty buffer returns 0.
The char conversion is retained; FF is -1 under the signed-char convention.
Returns the readable count n_w-n_r.
All five required fields exist.
Already-enabled objects report an error and are skipped; calloc zeros memory and initializes all fields correctly.
Nonfull buffers write modulo size and increment n_w; full buffers return 0 without overwriting.
Nonempty buffers read modulo size and increment n_r; empty buffers return 0.
Equality of the two counters determines emptiness.
Fullness requires a nonempty buffer with equal indices modulo size; zero size is guarded.
The counter difference is returned directly.
The realloc result is held temporarily; failure retains the old allocation and success updates size.
Contents are cleared and freed, fields are reset, and the buffer is disabled; NULL returns false.
Only buffer contents are memset; counters and configuration fields are unchanged.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
uint32_t addition by 1 provides 32-bit wraparound.

func1 passes the same argument to func2 and returns its result. D:72 explicitly allows an equivalent host C implementation; downgrading it for not delivering ARM LR instructions exceeds this task's scope.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
The required constant values are public; START/STOP are only defined, without frame recognition.
Motion/LED operations update the corresponding GPIO array indices with only 0/1.
The mask replaces only GPIOA_IDR bit 0.
Stored three-axis variables are returned through the shared read path.
Injected ADC data passes through the value adapter into the same formula.
ready/value are injected together, but host reads spin indefinitely when not ready.
Injection and the ISR reuse the same RXNE handler rather than creating separate queue logic.
TX-log characters are appended in order and length is incremented, with capacity protection.
A production single-step loop is provided without main or embedded self-tests.
The sole dynamic buffer has a release function; realloc failure preserves the original memory.
Null pointers, out-of-range indices, and full queues have explicit return paths.
The architecture retains raw bytes, no removal, no PWM, and ignored speed.

metric: coverage of 88 statically reviewable requirement leaves; 7 preclassified leaves unassessed
note: All 598 C-source lines and the 107-line header were read. Hardware-initialization stubs with no side effects are not credited as configuration merely because of their names.
scope_review_policy: R+D host-equivalent task contract; supplied A constrains shared-API methods; configuration stubs allowed, missing required values/paths not invented; Direct not penalized by unsupplied A; no candidate changes
scope_review_notes: R:1–16 and D:7–12 define project-level host-equivalent scope, not reconstruction of real upstream firmware.
D:11–12/A:273–276 allow configuration stubs; this does not waive R-specified configuration values/order.
D:72 allows transparent C semantics for host assembly functionality.
R:299 allocation-release obligation remains applicable regardless of hardware stub permissions.
Original standalone serializers record preliminary decisions; active JSON after this scope reconciliation is authoritative.

review_lineage.reason: Correct task scope interpretation consistently after reading R+D+A; preserve actual functional failures; not score selection.
